name: More Kuzhambu
subtitle: sour yogurt curry with ground coconut and cumin, never boiled

ingredients.note: fresh sweet yogurt gives a flat curry
okra or chow chow are the other usual choices
ground with the coconut; this is what stops the yogurt splitting
adds a rounder body to the paste
any more and the curry turns bitter
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the raw rice and toor dal together for 20 minutes so they grind smooth.
Take the yogurt out of the fridge early — cold yogurt hitting a hot pan splits immediately.
Whisk the yogurt with 1/2 cup water until there is no lump left anywhere.

steps.text: Simmer the ash gourd in 1 cup water with the turmeric and salt for 8 minutes, until translucent at the edges.
Grind the coconut, cumin, green chilli, soaked rice and toor dal with 1/2 cup water to a very smooth paste.
steps.tip: Any grit left in the paste will be obvious in the finished curry.

steps.text: Add the paste to the cooked gourd and simmer 6 minutes, until the raw rice smell disappears.
Take the pan off the heat and let it stop bubbling completely, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the whisked yogurt, stirring constantly as it goes.
Return to the lowest possible heat and warm it only until steam rises and it thickens slightly.
steps.tip: The moment it boils, the yogurt curdles into grains. Take it off before you think you should.

steps.text: Check the salt and take it off the heat entirely.
Heat the coconut oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the fenugreek, red chilli, curry leaves and hing.
steps.tip: Fenugreek burns black in seconds — add it after the mustard has finished popping.

steps.text: Pour the tempering over and serve with hot rice and a dry poriyal.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated and gets sourer. Reheat only to warm on the lowest heat, stirring; it will split if it boils.
